answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 48 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the comet hash is checked against the horizon checkpoint at intake, the sonnet audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 1908 identities would post 1173 proofs and burn roughly 28 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
